text: An MCP server that exposes any API, or groups of APIs, and does nothing on its own: plugins extend methods of an abstract base class that are called during tool reload, calls, responses and errors, while the core does the common proxy work.
Runs over stdio locally by default and can also run over streamable HTTP.
Well documented: README, concepts, plugin authoring guide covering small and big plugins, testing guide, configuration and transport reference, each with its own acceptance conditions.
Good examples of small and big plugins, runnable and tested: hello, single endpoint, a decorator multi-tool plugin with auth, a packaged OpenAPI plugin and a group-of-APIs config.
Plugins are very easy to implement: one class with one required hook, discovered from entry points or module:Class config entries, configured from one YAML file, testable in memory.
Python, uv, ruff, pytest, mise tasks lint and test, GitHub Actions CI; a new component at code/any-mcp with the public GitHub origin szymonrychu/any-mcp created after the gate.

Built on FastMCP 4.x (fastmcp>=4.1,<5) behind any-mcp's own plugin ABC with one adapter module; client tokens are never forwarded downstream; plugin exceptions become structured MCP tool errors; arguments are validated against schemas; correctness never relies on tools/list_changed.
v1 is tools only; released as the pinned git tag v0.1.0, installable via pip from git and consumed by the agent-orchestrator agent image.

Installable with pip the same way as claude-code-wrapper: a standard pyproject package with the console script any-mcp, installable via pip install any-mcp, pip install git+https://github.com/szymonrychu/any-mcp, pip install ., pipx install any-mcp and uv tool install any-mcp; any-mcp --version works; the README documents these; a test builds the wheel with uv build --wheel, installs it into a fresh venv and runs any-mcp --version. No PyPI publishing.

A plugin can ask the client for input mid-call (MCP 2026-07-28 InputRequiredResult) through one separate optional hook with a default that never requests input, wired through the FastMCP adapter and the call pipeline, documented in the authoring guide with an example, and tested over stdio and HTTP.
